metadata.note: The historical Houston-Dallas corridor of the Houston and Texas Central Railway (H&TC), later the Southern Pacific-controlled Texas & New Orleans Railroad (T&NO). The H&TC built north from Houston starting 1856, reaching Corsicana in 1871 and Dallas in 1872. SP's named passenger train the Sunbeam ran this route from 1925 (streamlined in 1937) until discontinued in 1957 -- well before Amtrak's 1971 creation, so this corridor was never inherited by Amtrak and no direct Houston-Dallas passenger train exists today (compare against amtrak.geojson, which routes through San Antonio instead). Geometry is a real-town waypoint approximation (Houston-Cypress-Hempstead-Navasota-Bryan-Hearne-Bremond-Kosse-Groesbeck-Corsicana-Ennis-Dallas), straight-line segments between towns known to be on or near the H&TC corridor -- NOT digitized from period track maps, so curvature within each town-to-town segment is still schematic rather than surveyed. Frequencies are estimated/unsourced except where noted. EXPANDED (2026-08-22) to cover the full H&TC system, not just the Houston-Dallas trunk: the 872-mile network (chartered 1848, construction from 1856) also reached Denison on the Red River in 1873 (connecting there with the MKT/'Katy' toward St. Louis), and had two major branches -- Hempstead-Brenham-Austin (predecessor Washington County Railroad completed Hempstead-Brenham April 1861; H&TC extended it to Austin, final spike Christmas Day 1871) and Bremond-Waco (via the acquired Waco and Northwestern Railroad, ex-'Waco Tap', completed 1872). Both branches connect to the already-modeled Houston-Dallas main line at Hempstead and Bremond respectively, both of which were already waypoints on that line. COLOR STANDARDIZATION (2026-08-22): all Houston and Texas Central Railway-branded features (main line, Dallas-Denison extension, Austin branch, Waco branch) now share color #9b2226, as the first step of a broader project to color-code every line on this map by operating company rather than by individual era/named-train. The Southern Pacific/Texas & New Orleans-era Sunbeam features keep their own distinct colors for now, since SP/T&NO was a different operator than H&TC itself.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_and_Texas_Central_Railway (chartered 1848, construction from 1856, Corsicana 1871, Dallas 1872, Denison 1873; later absorbed into Southern Pacific's Texas & New Orleans Railroad)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunbeam_(passenger_train) (T&NO/SP train, numbers 13/14; began 1925 as heavyweight, 6.5hr Houston-Dallas run per June 1926 and Aug 1937 timetables; streamlined Sept 19 1937 to a 4hr45min schedule over 264 miles; SP's companion train the Hustler dropped 1954; Sunbeam itself discontinued 1957)
https://www.american-rails.com/beam.html (timetable and consist detail corroborating the above)
https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/houston-and-texas-central-railway (TSHA Handbook of Texas entry on the H&TC's construction and corporate history)
https://hearnedepot.org/h-and-tc-railway/ (Hearne as an H&TC mainline station/junction)

https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/houston-and-texas-central-railway (872-mile system; Red River/Denison reached 1873; Washington County Railroad's Hempstead-Brenham completed April 1861, H&TC acquired it 1867 and extended to Austin, final spike Christmas Day 1871; Waco and Northwestern/'Waco Tap' acquired and Bremond-Waco completed 1872)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact station list and mileage for the full Houston-Dallas run; whether Groesbeck was actually a scheduled stop versus a nearby waypoint used only to approximate the curve toward Corsicana; whether other H&TC/SP named trains besides the Sunbeam and Hustler served this exact segment; precise launch date of the Hustler companion train. Exact discontinuation dates for the Denison extension, Austin branch, and Waco branch passenger service (all approximated here at 1925, the same year the Sunbeam launched on the main line, as a placeholder -- not independently confirmed for these branches).
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
